implementation_boundaries: This is a local browser slice, not a complete sandbox, authored story or finished game.
Field collecting is a route-and-containment simulation, not a freely navigable wilderness.
Hopper genetics use three independent diploid loci with fixed coefficients; no mutation, linkage, inherited morphology or general mating system.
Cicadas can be caught, assayed and prepared; a complete root-to-adult cicada breeding profile is not implemented.
The single nursery uses a conservative six-place commitment and fixed stage schedule, not the full general interval scheduler from W03.
Rates, costs, survival and stage lengths are prototype parameters; observed first-seed performance is not a profit guarantee.
Market renewal is explicit modeled off-screen customer funding; national NPC commerce, two-way retail, transport orders and contracts are not fully simulated.
Care credit prevents silent stock loss at zero funds; interest, creditor enforcement, general injury and lifetime care are future branches.
Native exchange is the W05 retained-cradle profile; broad tissue storage, regrowth and damage behavior remain open.
The unchanged two-racer path model retains its earlier aerodynamic, ground-only and entry-mass simplifications.
Cicada efficiency is stored as a selectable donor property but is NOT yet connected to the constant .75 race efficiency; current drive effect is cadence and force.
World JSON is user-editable local data, not competitive authority or protection from intentional cheating.
Archive bounds are 1200 specimen/component records, 200 broods, 15000 ledger entries and bounded world turns; world-scale performance is not established.
File and loopback HTTP navigation were blocked by this host. Exact HTML was exercised via set_content; native origin persistence and Windows/macOS launch remain unverified.
No human playtest or retention measurement. No final MIVIM numerical grade is claimed.

Reference.source_evidence_boundary: The screenshot does not disclose isolated part coefficients, a complete item catalogue, or every PCR installment. Build readings are not per-item effects.
reviewed_repairs: W06 stored cicada efficiency without using it. W07 compiles it into the same force/energy equations.
Frames, gears, stabilizers and independent suspension were not interchangeable current products. They now have donor/preparation/fit/race paths.

Native feet initially inherited a zero-release default, making ordinary tissue unrealistically unbeatable on that input. Native and legacy prepared foot baselines are explicit in W07, and selected stock is tested as a genuine full-circuit upgrade.
A donor-derived horn replacement initially bypassed the earlier yaw projection. The projection now applies to the measured reach.
Alternative preparations could otherwise duplicate a whole hind pair, mantis arms or larval fatbody. Region allocations enforce a physical choice; disjoint scarab and mole products remain allowed.
Live-stage expansion initially reused adult silhouettes in larval cards. The rendered cards and nursery now use stage-specific larval and pupal forms.
Long donor ids dominated product titles. The inspector separates recognizable product names from stable provenance metadata.
Two-column narrow shop cards compressed measurements. Narrow screens now use wider specimen and prepared-product cards.

The same shop could have funded an immediate unchanged retail-to-order buyback profit. Retail acquisition now exceeds that same-counter selected resale; preparation or real market differences remain legitimate value sources.

The inherited cumulative manifest described Wave 5 despite containing Wave 6. The new manifest explicitly records its current version and evidence; prior manifest remains in the byte-preserved baseline.

hopper.name: Switchyard hopper
hopper.sign: Paired release and clean recovery after a short hop.
hopper.seek: Keep synchronized legs to complement a high-return line; distance alone is misleading.

cicada.name: Furnace cicada
cicada.sign: Rhythmic loaded movement; intact thorax, not loudness.
cicada.seek: Select cadence, force and useful work per reserve unit independently. Efficiency now reaches the race.

scarab.name: Kilnback scarab
scarab.sign: Short loaded pushes; interlocking inner plates; do not grade by shell size.
scarab.seek: Strong support at ordinary mass creates frame stock; thick working muscles supply a different product.

mole.name: Ballast mole cricket
mole.sign: Intact short hip levers, toothed toes, grit-free joints.
mole.seek: Lowstep leverage serves loaded starts; purchase on ash supplies a separate contact product.

stick.name: Glassfoot stick insect
stick.sign: Pad attachment followed by release; inspect clean surfaces under comparable conditions.
stick.seek: Grip and release are distinct. A sticky but slow foot can bottleneck a high-cadence build.

wax.name: Reservoir waxmoth
wax.sign: Supported feeding larvae, not swollen recent gut contents; retain some to adulthood.
wax.seek: Harvest larval fatbody for energy OR a prepared damper. Adult breeders are not the same usable tissue stage.

fly.name: Sumpfly
fly.sign: Paired club-ended organs; controlled turns, not merely frantic flight.
fly.seek: Low signal delay permits an earlier correction through existing limbs. Sensors supply no free force.

mantis.name: Saltglass mantis
mantis.sign: Long useful reach with quick closure; isolate predatory stock in transit.
mantis.seek: Select fast closing arms for interception OR prepare the same limbs as disabled-attack counterbraces.

horn.name: Bullhorn beetle
horn.sign: Intact root and useful curve; long tips can conceal weak bases.
horn.seek: Preserve the horn-root assembly for attacks; separate head plates can become a browfoil.

moth.name: Ashveil moth
moth.sign: Intact margins and stiff light veins; resting inspection preserves surfaces.
moth.seek: Select high hold-down at modest drag, while retaining distinctive natural patterns for collectors.

hoppers.name: Grasshopper Hoppers
hoppers.purpose: One paired assembly carries launch and landing anatomy.

springknees.name: Locust Springknees
springknees.purpose: Fit landing couplers to native hind legs. A complete Hopper already contains this tissue; the two are alternative builds.

redline.name: Cicada Redline
redline.purpose: Cadence, force and conversion efficiency feed motion and energy consumption separately.

torque.name: Scarab Torque Bundle
torque.purpose: High force at lower cadence; ratio is still a separate component choice.

boxbrace.name: Scarab Boxbrace
boxbrace.purpose: Lateral structural support changes the corner load limit at an actual carried mass. Not an armor score.

lowstep.name: Mole-Cricket Lowstep
lowstep.purpose: A prepared leverage ratio multiplies the fine-tuning setting; force and free stride speed move in opposite directions.

cleats.name: Mole-Cricket Cleats
cleats.purpose: Mechanical purchase on loose ash differs from performance on smooth enamel.

sticktoe.name: Sticktoe Contact Set
sticktoe.purpose: Purchase limits slip; peel delay changes usable cadence. The same feet do not gain extra traction from a rarity label.

fatbody.name: Waxmoth Fatbody
fatbody.purpose: Capacity, delivery and loaded mass govern range and supplied power. Larva is the usable donor stage.

keel.name: Larval Keel
keel.purpose: The same larval tissue is allocated to a constrained damping assembly, not simultaneously to a second reservoir.

gyropods.name: Fly Gyropods
gyropods.purpose: Signal delay changes the correction rate supplied through available legs; no added force or armor.

catchclaws.name: Mantis Catchclaws
catchclaws.purpose: Reach and closure timing feed actual grasp attempts.

counterbraces.name: Mantis Counterbraces
counterbraces.purpose: Forelimbs are prepared as support-only lateral braces with grasp disabled. Added support competes with passing width.

bullhorn.name: Bullhorn Ram
bullhorn.purpose: Root-supported contact, reach and impact alter an aligned charge.

browfoil.name: Beetle Browfoil
browfoil.purpose: Prepared head-shell vanes add hold-down and real modeled drag; they do not grant flight.

splitvanes.name: Ashveil Split-Vanes
splitvanes.purpose: Light veined surfaces with selectable hold-down, drag and mass.

dry.name: Dry-bank nursery
dry.note: Paired running stock; six committed places.

root.name: Root-and-emergence cabinet
root.note: Root-fed juveniles then adult drive donors; seven-turn profile.

soil.name: Deep-soil nursery
soil.note: Burrowing young, pupation where required, protected emergence.

reed.name: Vertical molt case

predator.name: Partitioned predator case

limits: One named player host; alternative bodyforms, host breeding and purchasable whole-host kits are not yet implemented.
Ten fictional pair-bred donor profiles use three independent binary loci each. No colony genetics, mutation, linkage, continuous natural genotype or heritable appearance system.
The source screenshot establishes categories and aggregate build readings, not exact per-part formulas or complete game catalogues. Normalized RRR coefficients are authored.
Path-space two-racer ground simulation; root rectangles rather than swept limbs; no free 3D flight, full damage, steering physics or complete tire-like gait.
Structural support, sensory correction, release delay and rail-seam response are simplified mechanisms. Rail seams do not establish realistic suspension travel or mass-damper mechanics.
Prepared native replacement cradles remain a specific workshop profile. General graft rejection, storage decay, regrowth, aging and permanent loss are not decided by this implementation.
Waxmoth useful-stage and short vital-remains windows are implemented. Prepared components remain stable inventory; cold-chain storage and shipped-order transit remain open.
Three finite conversion kits and three finite selected orders. No unlimited item respawn, automatic contract renewal, full NPC supply simulation or national economy.
Market wallet renewal uses explicit off-screen customer funding. Repeated profiles are stress probes with supplied starting assets, not proof of profitability or fair comparisons of player careers.
Ordinary current-stock quotes use form and condition; individual project guidance beyond Hopper currently exposes trait evidence but is not a full multiform breeding optimizer.
User-editable local backups are consistency-checked, not secure multiplayer authority. Browser tests use exact HTML set_content because native navigation is blocked.
No Windows/macOS native file persistence, physical touch or human playtest; no measured enjoyment or retention; no final numerical MIVIM grade.

MIVIM.objective: An individually sourced or bred whole host carries its native geometry into personal kit assembly, persistent stable custody and the same racing system, with measurement-led component and lineage evidence.
MIVIM.comparator: One fixed roach recolored as several models; kit purchase spawns a fitted racer; each bench duplicates shared parts; names or rarity labels award synthetic performance.
MIVIM.numeric_grading: No authorized numerical scoring formula or weights are invented.

findings.quality: Implemented model, interactions and reviewed renders at declared local-prototype scope. Complete game and human usability gate open.
findings.novel_development_adherence: Concrete project-specific whole-organism, kit, ownership and evidence integration. No worldwide novelty claim.
findings.effectiveness: Demonstrated for tested body selection, purchased/caught/bred host registration, fitting, races, custody, backup and public evidence.
findings.creativity: Distinct whole-kit presentation and shared biological origin-to-racer path delivered; experiential originality remains unmeasured.
findings.scaling_potential: Reusable body/specimen profiles and shared command paths; a small local stable is not a large-world or multi-server benchmark.

MIVIM.supporting_work: Schema, reference checks, numerical parity and custody tests protect the intended integration. Their existence is not proof of fun or commercial success.

limitations: One local active world, multiple owned racers, and one selected player entry per two-racer ground event. No multi-player stable event or server authority.
Three discrete body plans plus three independent native loci. No blended anatomy, host personality learning, mutation, linkage or inherited appearance.
The host is one additional reproductive form beside ten existing donors. A discrete parental plan is not a species-level mating restriction.
Supported roots use simplified geometric bounds. No full articulated limb, swept collision, loaded muscle visualization or general multi-drive assembly.
Complete kit retail is implemented; player-manufactured full kits, sale of registered assembled racers, autonomous restocking and dynamic lineage pricing are not.
Measurement labels summarize twelve authored preparation profiles. Geometry-only parts and missing evidence are not forced into a tier. Thresholds and tier population are not calibrated.
Named lines report observed descendants and selected samples, not unbiased heritability estimates or guaranteed supply contracts.
Existing normalized path-space ground racing, simplified contact, reservoir mass at entry, and restricted reusable native cradles remain. Flight, broad storage decay and shipped orders are open.
Old HOST care has dedicated-cradle overhead; other living hosts occupy care and holding capacity. Opening money/facilities and supplier additions are disclosed endowments.
Local backup is editable user data, not anti-cheat. Native-file launch was blocked by the host; exact HTML was tested via set_content. Windows/macOS persistence and physical touch not verified.
No human playtest, retention measurement or full economic balance. MIVIM has no authorized numerical formula in the recovered requirements.

evidence.authority: Measured computational outputs and tests, not real biology, economy calibration or human playtest.

feltbrake.name: Moth-Felt Brake

railshoes.name: Beetle Railshoes
railshoes.pcr: Rollers and mounts / functional sliding analogue
railshoes.purpose: Rounded side-shell shoes carry a limited wall contact load with lower sliding loss. They are not rotating wheels, passive armor or a grip multiplier.

run.name: Gutter Run
run.description: Smooth straight. Extend a useful power run.

bend.name: Drum Bend
bend.description: Reversible quarter turn. The rails carry contact, not invisible lane locks.

rise.name: Brake Rise
rise.description: Raised approach engages a low pad, then launches from a low lip. Follow it with a straight landing run.

wash.name: Rivet Wash
wash.description: Landing seams exercise joints and separately fitted rebound tissue.

ash.name: Ash Gutter
ash.description: Same connectors; loose material changes the required foot purchase.

rail.name: Ribbed Rail Bend
rail.description: Quarter turn with a rough wall. Smooth guide tissue reduces contact loss.

kit.name: Apron / approach set
kit.purpose: Two donors, two separate contacts: slow at a raised approach and slide along a rail. Fit clearance yourself; no universal lap-time bonus.

limits: One local world and two-racer path-space ground races; no rigid-body limb physics, free aerial paths or lane-changing bridges.
Track editor is a snapped ordered chain of fixed dimensions and a conservative sampled planar-overlap check; not arbitrary free placement or a full terrain editor.

Passive Brake Rise uses a fixed normalized angle and height with simplified approach dynamics. An airborne arrival at a bend retires; no global death, destructive damage or retrieval simulation added.
Raised approach source is the physical Mini 4WD hobby layer, not an alleged additional Gaiden menu slot. No source-game numerical formula is invented.
Two new donor forms retain the limited three-independent-locus profile. No mutation, linkage, colony genetics, appearance heredity or full material science.
Rail contact is a limited-load planar friction proxy. Native corner response remains. Guide friction has no effect away from contact; passive shell stabilizers do not supply powered steering.
Prepared parts remain stable stock under the restricted reusable native-cradle model. Transport viability, broad graft removal and stage-preservation systems remain open.

One finite layout service, two finite new selected orders and one conversion set. Player-manufactured complete-kit selling, evidence-backed breeder commission acceptance and autonomous demand renewal are not delivered.
Fixed section prices, care, genotype coefficients and track dimensions are experimental. A tested profitable transaction or finish is not economic or retention calibration.

Local editable saves are consistency checked, not anti-cheat. File navigation blocked in test host; exact HTML set_content used. Native Windows/macOS storage, physical touch and human testing unverified.

rules.statement: Each rival has a particular host, particular donors and particular prepared components.
rules.purpose: The runner can be inspected as a real construction.

rules.statement: Compile NPCs with the player catalogue, fitting validation and compiler.
rules.purpose: Equivalent assembly uses equivalent mechanisms.

rules.statement: Publish the useful part measurements in the rival inspector.
rules.purpose: The player sees which observed property to investigate.

rules.statement: Rivals do not read unmeasured player genomes or conjure counterbuilds.
rules.purpose: Changing hidden player state cannot alter their current stock.

rules.statement: Role-specific mechanical advantages are not universal superiority.
rules.purpose: Leverage, load, reach and surface remain purposeful decisions.

rules.statement: NPC specimens are declared club-owned/competitor-owned fixture assets, not simulated prior breeding successes.
rules.purpose: No invented provenance or player ownership is granted.

rules.statement: A rival suggestion can become an existing selection target and field route.
rules.purpose: The suggestion preserves trait ID and changes neither genes nor inventory.

rules.statement: A meet announces equipment policy, course version, laps, opponents, format, purse, fees and qualification before entry.
rules.purpose: No hidden extra sporting requirement appears at settlement.

rules.statement: Entry uses an owned registered host with a committed valid build.
rules.purpose: An unresolved draft is not silently equipped or discarded.

rules.statement: Reserve the complete advertised purse before registration succeeds.
rules.purpose: Unfunded competition is unavailable rather than promising fictitious receipts.

rules.statement: One active meet is supported in the local implementation.
rules.purpose: A second registration cannot double-book the same world operation.

rules.statement: One host represents the player throughout that meet.
rules.purpose: Other stable projects remain available; changing the entrant requires withdrawal.

rules.statement: Between rounds the same host can be refitted and re-inspected.
rules.purpose: Already completed heats preserve their earlier snapshots.

rules.statement: The entered host cannot begin reproduction before its meet ends or is withdrawn.
rules.purpose: Competition and breeding share the same animal.

rules.statement: A pending calculation freezes requests and blocks conflicting world commands.
rules.purpose: No partly calculated round consumes a moving build or changing account.

rules.statement: Four entrants contest three round-robin rounds using the current two-racer engine.
rules.purpose: A roster of four is not falsely displayed as simultaneous four-roach physics.

rules.statement: Every pairing has two standing-start heats with swapped sides.
rules.purpose: Neither entrant permanently receives one favorable starting position.

rules.statement: Also reverse solver evaluation order in the second heat.
rules.purpose: The probe reduces order bias without claiming perfect physical symmetry.

rules.statement: Use 3 points for a valid heat win, 1 each for a valid tied finish and 0 for a loss or no finish.
rules.purpose: Contact and damage do not score championship points.

rules.statement: All-retired heats award no win and no tie point.
rules.purpose: Last-roach-standing does not replace completing the race.

rules.statement: Rank by points, then number of valid finishes; otherwise share rank.
rules.purpose: Arbitrary IDs or summed times across different rival encounters do not break the tie.

rules.statement: A qualifying crown requires first rank and at least three actual heat wins.
rules.purpose: An all-tied low-evidence table cannot automatically grant a championship invitation.

rules.statement: Results use identical frozen course and build inputs and required gate completion.
rules.purpose: Client place labels cannot override finishing times.

rules.statement: Four actual computed heats settle one round.
rules.purpose: NPC-versus-NPC results are simulated rather than inferred from labels.

rules.statement: First Current awards Local Open qualification; Ballast requires that record.
rules.purpose: Participation permission follows a real sporting result, not money or breeding rank.

rules.statement: A Regional win records Regional completion only.
rules.purpose: Factionals and World City remain explicitly not playable.

rules.statement: The custom-course invitational pays its declared purse but grants no championship qualification.
rules.purpose: A player-authored easy layout cannot manufacture official advancement.

rules.statement: Trophies preserve the entered host identity, name, meet and course version.
rules.purpose: Later renaming cannot rewrite the winner remembered by the record.

rules.statement: The first Local Open crown offers one actual donor pair from a finite nursery.
rules.purpose: The reward is useful stock, not a species or gene unlock.

rules.statement: The player chooses return-focused Hoppers or release-focused Glassfoot stock.
rules.purpose: Both connect to existing breeding and alternative-preparation projects.

rules.statement: Claiming requires two real holding places and protects the transferred stock.
rules.purpose: Full capacity does not delete the award or spawn overflow inventory.

rules.statement: Unchosen award stock remains with the club; a claimed ticket cannot pay again.
rules.purpose: No doubled offspring or second reward appears on retry.

rules.statement: The club receives a finite declared 1440-credit opening operating grant against the external account.
rules.purpose: Player cash and old account balances are preserved.

rules.statement: Registration fee goes to operating services; advertised prize funds are separately reserved.
rules.purpose: A registration receipt is not a prize receipt.

rules.statement: A completed round costs two credits plus actual care and advances two world turns.
rules.purpose: Broods, care, orders and competition share one clock.

rules.statement: The six-heat player schedule covers three rounds and six world turns.
rules.purpose: Mirror-leg playback is not another attendance charge.

rules.statement: Tied entrants split the prize slots they occupy; indivisible remainder returns to the club.
rules.purpose: Conservation holds without silently creating fractions or extra money.

rules.statement: NPC prize shares enter their actual accounts.
rules.purpose: The player cannot take every advertised placing reward.

rules.statement: Cancellation of a failed calculation pays no round fee; withdrawal retains incurred costs and refunds the unawarded purse to the club.
rules.purpose: Technical failure and voluntary withdrawal have distinct consequences.

rules.statement: The event roster has finite sponsored editions: three per official card and two custom exhibitions.
rules.purpose: There is no unfunded infinite prize renewal; practice and existing livelihoods remain.

rules.statement: Replay, scrubbing, historical inspection and donor-project inspection cost no world time.
rules.purpose: Learning and replay do not mint prizes or repeat care charges.

rules.statement: Official meetings use their published normalized club geometry.
rules.purpose: The same course version is used by all entrants in that meeting.

rules.statement: An invitational freezes the currently laid owned circuit.
rules.purpose: Drafts, saved plans and privately missing pieces cannot stand in for a physical course.

rules.statement: A player course cannot be republished while its invitational is active.
rules.purpose: The floor does not change under a pending meeting.

rules.statement: A setup on smooth short circuits may differ from a longer loose-surface Regional.
rules.purpose: Traits and fitting, not a regional stat aura, explain changed results.

rules.statement: Event cards expose their useful rules and geometry before charging.
rules.purpose: The player knows the goal, current entrants and costs.

rules.statement: A current-round board keeps points, valid finishes, next opponent and fitted identity together.
rules.purpose: The event remains readable beside the actual roach.

rules.statement: Rival portraits draw their committed component layouts using the existing anatomical renderer.
rules.purpose: Inspection is not a generic rival icon beside invented stats.

rules.statement: The result comes before diagnosis and supply suggestions.
rules.purpose: Winning the race remains the central achievement.

rules.statement: Race replays use real current calculations and frozen appearance.
rules.purpose: No preselected win animation stands in for simulation.

rules.statement: Portable backups preserve tables, requests, qualification and reward custody, but not session replay frames.
rules.purpose: Restored history never claims that missing playback data exists.

rules.statement: Source-derived guidance is optional.
rules.purpose: Buying a coordinated kit and simply racing remains a complete participation path.

rules.statement: Use current behavior checks, original-release regression, rendered review and human testing as distinct evidence categories.
rules.purpose: Tests cannot become a claim of enjoyment or originality.

rules.statement: Preserve old cumulative records and original source references in the release.
rules.purpose: Missing Wave10 runtime is recorded, not covered with a fabricated preservation claim.

rules.statement: No final numeric MIVIM grade or acronym expansion is invented.
rules.purpose: Quality and novel-development adherence remain non-compensable gates.

rules.statement: Treat local backups as user-editable consistency-checked data, not server-authoritative competition records.
rules.purpose: Synthetic settlement tests do not establish anti-cheat.

rules.statement: Carry unverified Hopper timing and multi-racer-motion fidelity as explicit future tests.
rules.purpose: No extra jump-win bonus masks a weak actual interaction.

event_definitions.name: First Current
event_definitions.purpose: The first official Open circuit title. Win the meet to earn an invitation to the Regional trial.

event_definitions.name: Glassline Dash
event_definitions.purpose: Weapon-free builds, real contact and legal Hoppers. Raw pace, release and reserve matter.

event_definitions.name: Sparks at Sundown
event_definitions.purpose: Working offense and light carapace. Win by finishing races, not by attack count.

event_definitions.name: Ballast Regional Trial
event_definitions.purpose: A longer loose-surface circuit. A win records Regional completion; Factional racing is not implemented.

event_definitions.name: Your Circuit Invitational
event_definitions.purpose: Host real races on the frozen version of your owned layout. Custom geometry never grants a championship qualifier.

rival_definitions.name: SEAMSTRESS
rival_definitions.purpose: Clean release and fast correction. The legs must disengage fast enough to use the drive.

rival_definitions.name: THIRD NOTICE
rival_definitions.purpose: Matched takeoff and controlled recovery. Supply, launch tissue and rebound tissue are distinct.

rival_definitions.name: BOLT MUNCHER
rival_definitions.purpose: Usable thrust and loose-ground feet under a supported heavy body. More leverage is not always faster.

rival_definitions.name: HORN TAX
rival_definitions.purpose: Forceful aligned charges. Horn geometry only works when the roach reaches contact.

rival_definitions.name: COUNTEROFFER
rival_definitions.purpose: Fast closure at working reach. Interception is an action with timing, not passive armor.

rival_definitions.name: FLASHLEG
rival_definitions.purpose: A narrow passing body with a forward attack. The same drive supplies racing and contact.

rules.observable: A tin does not stop biological obligations.

rules.statement: Opening releases the same host and components and does not equip them.
rules.decision: Assemble personally after unpacking.
rules.observable: The guide creates a draft; fitting still commits the real construction.

rules.statement: Maker retail transfers all existing kit contents without cloning them.
rules.decision: Buy the same delivered product from Two Nets.
rules.observable: The original donor identities reach the recipient bench and race.

rules.statement: Opened supplier receipts remain history rather than perpetual ownership constraints.
rules.decision: Reuse or sell a previously opened native host appropriately.
rules.observable: An old receipt neither blocks legitimate packing nor reopens to restore missing assets.

rule_groups.name: BREEDER / purposeful evidence and living delivery

rules.statement: A breeder request names a donor form, measured contribution and actual living delivery.
rules.decision: Supply synchronization or release for another breeding project.
rules.observable: The request does not accept prepared tissue instead of reproductive stock.

rules.statement: Customer evidence evaluates its own target rather than blindly trusting the line’s selected label.
rules.decision: Use relevant recorded observations.
rules.observable: A renamed line does not rewrite or satisfy unrelated customer requirements.

rules.statement: Count distinct tested descendants, matching descendants and distinct measured broods separately.
rules.decision: Develop enough useful observed evidence.
rules.observable: Repeated tests of one individual or many siblings do not create several broods.

rules.statement: Untested observed descendants remain unknown; unopened future outcomes do not enter the report.
rules.decision: Assay only when the information is useful.
rules.observable: The interface cannot reveal hidden survival or convert missing evidence into failure or success.

rules.statement: Sold or prepared descendants can remain historical evidence with their actual custody.
rules.decision: Keep useful records after commercial use.
rules.observable: Evidence does not recreate owned stock.

rules.statement: The delivered pair must itself be owned, intact, mature, measured, unreserved and composed of compatible A/B roles.
rules.decision: Choose eligible descendants from the line.
rules.observable: A strong evidence report cannot bypass unavailable or unsuitable living animals.

rules.statement: Both delivered animals must satisfy the customer contribution.
rules.decision: Supply relevant future breeders, not arbitrary members of a famous line.
rules.observable: A compatible pair alone does not fulfill a synchronization promise.

rules.statement: Protected delivery animals require scoped confirmation; original founders are not implicitly sold.
rules.decision: Select exactly which reproductive assets to transfer.
rules.observable: The two delivered identities change owner while the source line remains.

rules.statement: A delivery freezes the narrow evidence claim that was accepted.
rules.decision: Retain receipt counts and sampled-brood identities.
rules.observable: Selected measured descendants are not reported as an unbiased future yield or a race-win guarantee.

rules.statement: Failure and inconvenient reproductive-role distributions remain real outcomes.
rules.decision: Retry, source another contribution or decline a commitment.
rules.observable: The browser test preserves an all-A early brood and a failed attempt instead of spawning a convenient pair.

rule_groups.name: DEMAND / useful products and earned income

rules.statement: Two complete-kit briefs and two breeder briefs coexist with ordinary immediate trade.
rules.decision: Supply a construction, a breeding contribution or surplus.
rules.observable: A casual racer need not become a certified breeder.

rules.statement: Accepting an order reserves actual buyer funds but pays no seller.
rules.decision: Accept a feasible commitment.
rules.observable: Escrow, current cash and hoped-for income remain distinct.

rules.statement: Accepted delivery transfers all promised assets and payment together.
rules.decision: Complete a whole-kit or pair handover.
rules.observable: Retries cannot duplicate funds, hosts or components.

rules.statement: Local deadlines are inclusive; later expiry returns unearned funds.
rules.decision: Hand over actual stock at the counter within the displayed window.
rules.observable: No shipping system is implied by a local due date.

rules.statement: Completed repeatable briefs can offer their next bounded edition when the buyer can fund it.
rules.decision: Produce another physical kit rather than repeat a receipt.
rules.observable: No infinite customer or immediate income is created by renewal.

rules.statement: An owner may publish an actual champion’s recorded round and request one specific showroom inquiry per meet.
rules.decision: Translate public interest into a new product goal.
rules.observable: An alternate host and stock must satisfy the published promise before payment.

rules.statement: Champion inquiries are finite authored counter opportunities, not simulated mass popularity.
rules.decision: Use the disclosed two-edition limit and funding.
rules.observable: The race trophy itself neither adds a genetic bonus nor pays product income.

rules.statement: Delivered sealed maker kits appear as the same assets on the main Two Nets shelf.
rules.decision: Buy, supply or inspect actual commercial inventory.
rules.observable: A separate maker view cannot hide a second cloned shop instance.

rules.statement: Retail quotes consider already posted same-counter kit buyback prices.
rules.decision: Pay for stock or add real production value.
rules.observable: An unchanged newly purchased kit cannot immediately profit against a currently posted request from the same counter.

rules.statement: Operating costs, capital, retained stock, gross receipts and cash changes remain distinct.
rules.decision: Compare a completed project honestly.
rules.observable: The tested first manufacturing route may lose cash despite a successful sale.

rules.statement: Claimed line reliability is supported by observations rather than a price aura.
rules.decision: Seek a useful customer and deliver accepted stock.
rules.observable: A new name or qualification label does not autonomously increase every buyer’s price.

rule_groups.name: PRESENT / useful decisions in one hobby

rules.statement: The maker counter leads with the actual proposed animal and recognizable parts.
rules.decision: See the product before inspecting details.
rules.observable: The same anatomy renderer serves bench, maker and kit shelf.

rules.statement: Reference construction, printed requirements, selected stock and physical tin are separate visible stages.
rules.decision: Identify the next meaningful action.
rules.observable: A published recipe is not styled as already-owned product inventory.

rules.statement: Each rejected stock item states the relevant measurement, fit, ownership or reservation cause.
rules.decision: Repair the correct issue.
rules.observable: Unmeasured is not confused with genetically poor, and fitted elsewhere is not incompatible.

rules.statement: Per-measurement and placement controls are optional depth with explicit keyboard-friendly inputs.
rules.decision: Choose coarse starting promises or detailed tuning.
rules.observable: Precision dragging and allele notation are not required to make a kit.

rules.statement: Donor-route and contribution actions use the same existing project and field identities.
rules.decision: Find the anatomy the product lacks.
rules.observable: A range mismatch above the upper bound suggests less, not automatically more.

rules.statement: Line evidence and live delivery selectors remain beside the actual customer.
rules.decision: Inspect the evidence gap and eligible animals together.
rules.observable: Count labels explicitly say measured broods and unmeasured descendants.

rule_groups.name: CONTINUITY / scoped quality and preserved history

rules.statement: Migration appends maker state without granting player cash or rerolling stock.
rules.decision: Continue existing saves.
rules.observable: W11 data is preserved except declared schema/profile changes; no W10 executable migration is invented.

rules.statement: Restore synchronizes the selected world catalogue before maker validation.
rules.decision: Restore a legitimate alternate world.
rules.observable: Previously viewed fixtures cannot cause stale descriptor validation failures.

rules.statement: World backup and product export have different authority.
rules.decision: Restore local world state explicitly or export only knowledge.
rules.observable: Consistency checking is not secure multiplayer authority.

rules.statement: The existing race, bench, artwork, club and circuit source bodies stay unchanged.
rules.decision: Extend production without replacing existing racing.
rules.observable: No movement fidelity or new tournament stage is credited to this wave.

rules.statement: Required quality and novel-development adherence remain noncompensable gates.
rules.decision: Assess the implemented contribution at its scope.
rules.observable: Test count, output length and speed do not establish novelty or enjoyment.

rules.statement: Effectiveness, creativity and scaling potential retain separate evidence states.
rules.decision: Carry human, platform and economy gaps forward.
rules.observable: An actual browser route does not establish world-scale performance or guaranteed profit.

Physical packed host and anatomy, later opened historical receipt. Proposed entry is not an actual race result.
Buyer terms stay fixed. Receipt is earned only on accepted actual stock.
Frozen selected-sample evidence; not statistical future guarantee or new specimen ownership.
Owner-selected actual history; one specific inquiry per meet. No invented earlier or future race.
One delivery edition, one payment and exact transferred assets; no replay renewal.

world_threads.runtime: Implemented local transactions and recipient controls; NPC retail uptake not simulated.

world_threads.runtime: Implemented through Two Nets delegated buyer wallet.

path: running pads or alternative brake preparation
world_threads.value: The same inherited material can serve racing construction and a customer’s future breeding project.
world_threads.runtime: Existing source/preparation paths and new stock/claim matching; not a new insect or mutation system.

world_threads.value: Public construction information has a useful commercial follow-through without claiming genetics caused a win.
world_threads.runtime: Owner publication and authored showroom request; no automatic regional news diffusion.

repairs.before: Mole mechanical advantage was labeled globally higher-better.
repairs.after: The catalogue marks a target range; maker matching gives the appropriate missing direction only outside the operating band.
repairs.enables: Gear selection stays about useful delivery rather than a false tier ladder.

repairs.before: One generic tolerance encouraged treating unrelated promises alike.
repairs.after: Explicit min/max requirements per measured native or prepared property; known axes, domain and source coverage validated.
repairs.enables: Quick release and sufficient loose-ground purchase can be specified independently.

repairs.before: Legacy component records omit fields that their compiler still uses.
repairs.after: Published observations include the exact declared legacy defaults without altering race code or claiming a new assay.
repairs.enables: Old earned components can be honest recipe references.

repairs.before: A previously opened supplier-kit record required its host to remain registered indefinitely.

repairs.enables: A real host can participate in later legitimate manufacturing and resale.

repairs.after: A public quote covers eligible current kit-order buyback plus the declared 24-credit margin.

limits: Maker code is a new reconstruction on recovered Wave11, not the missing Wave10 executable. Its written handoff remains in history.
No new donor form, mutation, linkage, inherited appearance or full reproductive simulation is added. Existing thirteen-form authored quantitative profiles supply products.

Product recipes retain one reference body plan, explicit native promises and fixed reference setup. Alternate-host-plan adaptation, formal revision series and user-selectable arbitrary substitution groups remain open.
Prototype margins are 0/10/15/25 percent starting conveniences; individual measured bounds override them. They are neither calibrated manufacturing tolerances nor statistical confidence.
The historical HOST remains on its nontransferable starter cradle. Pack another owned mature host; a parked registered host must first be native-only and free of prepared drafts.
No generic sale of a currently assembled active racer. This release sells packed build-it-yourself kits and specific living breeder pairs.

Four finite named briefs share the actual Two Nets wallet; institutional names describe authored customer purposes rather than fully independent national accounts. Owner-approved champion inquiries are bounded authored opportunities, not autonomous information diffusion.
All deliveries are local counter transfers. Prepared-stock decay, shipping, temperature-chain logistics, general injury, aging and regrowth remain unchanged or open.
Packed care uses the current simplified holding/upkeep branch. A paid receipt is not proof of balanced prices, sustainable demand or affordable growth.

The first complete browser manufacturing project loses cash after its win; retained breeders, samples and reference racer are assets, not sale revenue. Comparative multi-cohort careers require further calibration.
The two-roach race operators and club structure are unchanged. Hopper timing, articulated motion, true multi-roach physics, Flyer routes, Factionals and World City remain open.
Recipient construction is exercised by buying back the same kit through actual controls. Autonomous NPC assembly, racing with purchased maker stock and individual customer AI are not implemented.
Local product export has no importer in this wave. Whole-world restore is consistency checked, user editable, and not competitive server authority.
The shared global catalogue serves one active local world. No multi-world service or large-world benchmark is established.

Browser verification used exact HTML set_content after native file navigation was blocked. Native Windows/macOS origin persistence, physical touch, human usability, engagement and retention remain unverified.

evidence.scope: Measured test results are regenerated independently of this source specification. Browser routes use ordinary funds and actual controls; nonbrowser fixtures disclose synthetic working capital.

manifest.title: LUCKY 13 — Wildlands Expeditions
manifest.serialization: Strict JSON .spec; RRR exchange format, not an invented canonical private MIVIM grammar

sources.title: Tamiya — Mini 4WD Setup Guide
sources.scope: Separate motor output, gearing, contact, brakes, rebound and builder adjustments.
sources.limit: Physical Mini 4WD, not natural insect mechanics or unpublished PCR item equations.

sources.title: SEGA — Gaiden Pocket Circuit
sources.scope: Pocket Circuit venue, car-body/part acquisition, Time Attack and local rivals.
sources.limit: Other activities on the same webpage are not Pocket Circuit evidence; field expeditions are RRR extensions.

sources.title: Canadian Museum of Nature — Collecting Insects with an Ear to the Ground
sources.scope: Different collecting techniques sample different microhabitats; leaf-litter sifting, nets, light traps and vegetation sampling serve specific searches.
sources.limit: No museum specimen-killing method, tropical rarity percentage or actual husbandry prescription is imported into the game.

sources.title: Mewgenics — developer-authored Steam description
sources.scope: Resource expeditions, returning animals, inherited properties, breeding and facility investment participate in one progression system.
sources.limit: No exact genetics, capture algorithm, probabilities or cause of retention attributed to Mewgenics.

selection_review.reason: The weakest directly playable acquisition link was route-button collection. Spatial source selection can feed the already working genomes, anatomy, stock, kits, money and racing without inventing unrelated score progression.

selection_review.candidate: Universal Lucky 13 bonus or rarity wheel
selection_review.reason: Would bypass purposeful parts and turn the expansion into a probability reward disconnected from material selection.
Still a valid large expansion, but requires dedicated aerial locomotion, source anatomy and course validation. No ground race reskin is acceptable.
Novel morphology remains a future option; extra labels without new assembly/action mechanisms would not meet this expansion objective.

Reference.authority: Author canon governs. Source facts inform functions; invented RRR world values remain explicit proposals.
Reference.previous_queue: W13 active-limb task carried rather than falsely closed; latest user authorized a researched core expansion.

verge.name: Switchyard Reclamation
verge.subtitle: Spring tissue · hip leverage · living foundations
verge.description: The old routes open into connected feeding margins, ballast shelters and warm service recesses. Useful stock is not restricted to one species per trip.

glass.name: The Overglass
glass.subtitle: Contact pads · grasping arms · brake material
glass.description: Vertical growing frames alternate with exposed glass and sheltered textile lofts. Look for usable anatomy in motion; approach it where that anatomy is supported.

kiln.name: Cooling Works
kiln.subtitle: Drive tissue · structural plates · reserves · rail shoes
kiln.description: Root galleries and cooling compost supply power donors. Feed cavities contain stage-sensitive reserve stock; smooth underpipe surfaces carry guide donors.

v-bank.name: Split-sleeper bank
v-bank.clue: Paired landing impressions beside the grass lip.
v-bank.purpose: Synchronization founders for an existing high-return line; complete Hoppers or alternative joints.

v-ballast.name: Ballast trench
v-ballast.clue: Short burrows and broad toe scrapes between stones.
v-ballast.purpose: Loose-ground contact and hip delivery; allocate toes and hip levers separately.

v-culvert.name: Service culvert
v-culvert.clue: Flattened molt cases under the warm return pipe.
v-culvert.purpose: A new host, unrelated native stock, or ordinary whole-stock sales.

v-pole.name: Rooted signal pole
v-pole.clue: Empty emergence cases above rooted cable channels.
v-pole.purpose: Drive cadence or separate sensing stock; activity does not establish efficiency.

g-wall.name: Dewglass wall
g-wall.clue: Repeated pad attachment and peel marks on glazed leaves.
g-wall.purpose: Quick-release feet to complement high-purchase stock; the same pads can instead make a brake strip.

g-frame.name: Hanging frames
g-frame.purpose: Fast closure at useful reach, or a support-only conversion from the same arms.

g-loft.name: Felt loft
g-loft.clue: Resilient ventral folds and intact resting wing margins.
g-loft.purpose: Brake compression or low-resistance aero material; preserve the surface you came for.

g-seep.name: Seep ledges
g-seep.clue: Short correction flights above sheltered feed residue.
g-seep.purpose: Fast sensing or reserve larvae; useful-stage stock has a different role from reproductive adults.

k-root.name: Root furnace
k-root.clue: Repeated working movement near the coolest sap channels.
k-root.purpose: Efficiency complements a high-cadence line. A field glimpse cannot certify work per reserve unit.

k-bed.name: Cooling compost
k-bed.clue: Load-bearing shell ribs and rooted debris furrows.
k-bed.purpose: Supported drive, separate structural plates, or a root-supported ram.

k-feed.name: Insulation larder
k-feed.clue: Supported feeding larvae and closed pupation sleeves.
k-feed.purpose: Fatbody for a reservoir OR a damper; retain some larvae to become adult founders.

k-apron.name: Underpipe apron
k-apron.clue: Smooth shell glances between abrasive ledges.
k-apron.purpose: Low-loss supported rail guides or separate loose-ground feet; these are different contacts.

padded.name: Three-cell specimen case
padded.description: Individual supported cells. No added transfer risk; the capture tool still matters. Carry three.

divided.name: Four-cell field case
divided.description: Four separate cups. Small transfer risk for exposed limbs and membranes.

bulk.name: Six-cell haul case
bulk.description: More ordinary stock. Delicate anatomy faces a declared handling risk; genes never change.

cup.name: Soft capture cup
cup.description: Close, careful collection. Reliable when an insect is exposed and settled.

sweep.name: Short sweep net
sweep.description: Longer reach; particularly useful in foliage. Fast but less protective of delicate anatomy.

sleeve.name: Split reed sleeve
sleeve.description: Enclose the supporting perch. Strong on vertical stems and sheltered surfaces.

NOTES.hopper: Paired release watched during a short natural hop; surface and posture can influence the screen.
NOTES.mole: Toe purchase watched on this patch, not on every course surface.
NOTES.roach: Native proportions observed in a moving animal; exact mass requires the workshop.
NOTES.cicada: Visible contraction rhythm is a cadence screen, not an efficiency assay.
NOTES.stick: Attachment and peel watched on this surface; moisture can confound the screen.
NOTES.mantis: Closing response watched at the current reach; no forced maximum strike.
NOTES.fly: Corrective response observed; host-interface performance still needs testing.
NOTES.wax: Reserve-region outline inspected; recent feeding can confound apparent storage.
NOTES.scarab: Plate support observed during a natural push; mass remains unmeasured.
NOTES.horn: Horn geometry observed; it does not certify root strength.
NOTES.moth: Intact surface proportions inspected; aerodynamic work is not measured here.
NOTES.darkling: A glancing passage is a surface screen, not a calibrated friction measurement.
NOTES.feltmoth: Fold compression observed under the animal’s own movement; final fit remains separate.

rules.statement: Wildlands expands how the existing racing anatomy is acquired; it does not replace racing with a separate loot game.
rules.decision: Select a useful component contribution before seeking a source.
rules.observable: The same prepared properties reach the unchanged racing compiler.

rules.statement: Lucky 13 names the expansion, not a new universal luck statistic.
rules.decision: Choose a route, method and specimen rather than buy a luck aura.
rules.observable: No new rarity or lucky-sect multiplier affects race output.

rules.statement: Keep Gaiden menu/mode evidence, physical Mini 4WD mechanisms, real field-method inspiration and RRR fiction separate.
rules.decision: Use the correct source for a design claim.
rules.observable: No capture probability or genome model is described as a PCR rule.

rules.statement: The latest expansion request deliberately reprioritizes spatial collecting ahead of the previous motion queue.
rules.decision: Develop an interconnected core gap.
rules.observable: Hopper loading and full articulated racing remain explicitly carried work.

rules.statement: Existing quick collection routes and shop purchases remain valid.
rules.decision: Choose depth of field participation.
rules.observable: Detailed expeditions are not a new permission or mandatory profession.

rules.statement: Current habitats contain thirteen existing forms; this is not thirteen newly invented species.
rules.decision: Reuse their functioning supply, breeding and preparation paths.
rules.observable: The catalogue and old genomes are not reset.

rules.statement: Three connected districts contain twelve authored habitat patches.
rules.decision: Select a district with useful sources and travel along its edges.
rules.observable: A remote node cannot be reached by a disconnected move.

rules.statement: Each patch names plausible source forms, visible signs, useful anatomy and a selection purpose.
rules.decision: Look for the missing trait or ordinary sale stock.
rules.observable: A route is more specific than a generic random-rarity chest.

rules.statement: Each patch creates six distinct canonical specimens in a bounded cohort.
rules.decision: Find individuals already present.
rules.observable: Lures and repeated viewing do not generate another insect.

rules.statement: Population traits are sampled before capture and independently of the active breeding goal.
rules.decision: Observe and select; do not reroll by changing the project.
rules.observable: Changing a target does not rewrite genes or secretly supply its perfect solution.

rules.statement: Authored habitat distributions can favor one contribution without guaranteeing a desirable combination.
rules.decision: Choose where to seek founders.
rules.observable: Capture itself applies no location-based stat buff.

rules.statement: The expedition pins its district cohort epoch.
rules.decision: Revisit a patch during the same outing.
rules.observable: Crossing a world-time cycle cannot regenerate its stock mid-trip.

rules.statement: A later expedition may create a new authored cohort; previous individuals remain historical records.
rules.decision: Return for later stock while retaining pedigree and origin.
rules.observable: Archived population members cannot be captured through stale commands.

rules.statement: Legacy quick-route plots and new spatial patches have separate declared population records.
rules.decision: Choose the representation useful for this session.
rules.observable: No globally simulated shared food web is falsely claimed.

rules.statement: The field is a discrete nine-by-six patch with obstacles, cover and clear sight.
rules.decision: Choose reachable positions rather than select remote capture buttons.
rules.observable: A tool needs the actual current candidate within range and line of sight.

rules.statement: Quiet and rapid approaches consume different numbers of field beats.
rules.decision: Trade elapsed care and opportunity against disturbance.
rules.observable: Fast arrival can disturb nearby animals; it does not reduce their genetic quality.

rules.statement: Cover reduces the disturbance caused by a fast approach into it.
rules.decision: Use the geometry rather than an invisible stealth-level check.
rules.observable: Cover does not replace actual line-of-sight or tool reach.

rules.statement: Resting, foraging, sheltering, approaching, feeding and alert states influence access.
rules.decision: Wait, reposition or attract existing stock.
rules.observable: An alerted animal can move and become more difficult to secure.

rules.statement: A close cup, longer sweep and split reed sleeve have different reach, terrain fit and anatomy risks.
rules.decision: Pack two tools suited to the intended source.
rules.observable: Longer reach is not identical to better preservation.

rules.statement: Compatible rations or prey decoys attract only individuals already in the patch.
rules.decision: Create a better approach opportunity.
rules.observable: A lure changes position and accessibility, not species or genotype.

rules.statement: Three lure charges and a seven-beat lure lifetime are declared outing resources.
rules.decision: Decide where the setup is worth spending.
rules.observable: Repeated placement spends supplies; leaving the browser idle does not consume them.

rules.statement: Approaching insects cannot all occupy the same current field cell.
rules.decision: Read individual targets near a lure.
rules.observable: A crowd is not rendered as one unusable stack of overlapping capture markers.

rules.statement: Capture outcome uses tool conditions and an individual attempt counter, separate from heredity.
rules.decision: Choose a method with visible limitations.
rules.observable: Failed capture leaves the same individual in its population, possibly disturbed.

rules.statement: Pupae remain immobile while their stage is recorded as pupa.
rules.decision: Recognize the current usable stage.
rules.observable: The generic foraging routine cannot make a pupa chase bait.

rules.statement: Three-, four- and six-place cases have distinct declared handling risks.
rules.decision: Choose careful individual stock or larger ordinary volume.
rules.observable: Risk attaches to real anatomy, not a rarity-weight capacity system.

rules.statement: Departure reserves the whole selected case capacity at home before travel begins.
rules.decision: Plan around active production.
rules.observable: A repeating brood cannot occupy holding promised to incoming catches.

rules.statement: A secured specimen becomes player-owned in the canonical inventory immediately.
rules.decision: Keep track of the actual animal in transit.
rules.observable: Captured stock is not copied from a temporary field inventory on return.

rules.statement: Capturing one animal replaces one empty case reservation with one living care obligation.
rules.decision: Fill the prepared case.
rules.observable: Occupied plus reserved space remains consistent.

rules.statement: Handling damage affects a named anatomical region without changing inherited potential.
rules.decision: Distinguish immediate donor use from reproductive contribution.
rules.observable: A damaged desired part does not imply that every gene became worse.

rules.statement: Intact optional cargo may be released at its source patch.
rules.decision: Make room for another find deliberately.
rules.observable: Ownership and working custody change without creating another animal.

rules.statement: Returned specimens remain protected until the player chooses their purpose.
rules.decision: Assay, retain, breed, prepare or sell.
rules.observable: Ordinary automatic production does not silently liquidate the expedition.

rules.statement: Transit work reservations clear on return while specimen and expedition provenance remain.
rules.decision: Use the existing workshop again.
rules.observable: No extra copy is needed to place the catch in a breeding project.

rules.statement: An optional field screen describes one observed phenotype contribution.
rules.decision: Investigate the relevant anatomy.
rules.observable: The screen is neither an exact value nor a complete genotype readout.

rules.statement: The screen includes fixed individual observation error and contextual limitations.
rules.decision: Treat the clue as a reason to inspect, not a certificate.
rules.observable: Field humidity, surface and posture are acknowledged uncertainties rather than measured environmental simulation.

rules.statement: Repeated observation of the same individual does not reroll its screen.
rules.decision: Seek more useful evidence through the actual assay path.
rules.observable: Staring repeatedly cannot guarantee a favorable reading.

rules.statement: The public field view contains visible candidates, not all unseen positions or genetic objects.
rules.decision: Explore from observable information.
rules.observable: Changing unseen alleles does not change unobserved capture advice or tool success estimates.

rules.statement: The existing paid assay and preparation protocols remain responsible for exact part measurements.
rules.decision: Decide whether to buy information before committing tissue.

limits: A turn-based patch expedition with 3 district graphs and 12 nine-by-six boards, not a freely navigable continuous open world.
Thirteen existing forms. No new species, extra lucky gene, mutation, linkage, learned behavior or inherited appearance implemented.
Authored habitat probabilities, capture thresholds, action times and equipment are prototype parameters, not measured ecology or real handling instructions.
Wild behavior is discrete local movement and accessibility. No full food web, weather simulation, predation or unbounded regional population engine.
Legacy quick-route plots and spatial patches are separate authored population sources; not one globally unified wildlife model.
Current-world archive bounds still apply. Wild specimens remain records; long campaigns may reach the bounded archive and need subsequent compaction design.
Field equipment is a loaned outing loadout bundled into the fee, not a complete gear-manufacturing or purchasing progression.
No new paid exploration tasks or auto-selling scout results. Existing ordinary trade, selected orders and maker operations are used.
Prepared tissue uses earlier stable-stock/reusable-collar rules. General storage decay, donor welfare, aging, regrowth and permanent loss remain earlier explicit decisions.
Four-entry club rosters still use paired ground heats. Race operators remain byte-identical to W12; no airborne-fidelity improvement is claimed.
Browser uses exact HTML after file navigation was blocked. Linux Chromium coverage does not establish Windows/macOS native-file storage, physical touch or human usability.
32 supply runs are bounded automated policies with different tools/cases, not fair full-career comparisons, causal tool estimates or a guaranteed profit curve.

Evidence.scope: Automated model cases and actual browser controls are separate. Tests do not measure retention, human usability or fun.

sections.title: 1. Reading authority and the scope of this volume
sections.intro: This is a reference-book expansion, not a new executable release. Earlier experiments remain useful evidence and historical artifacts. The chapters below define objects, relationships, observable behavior and creative intent before downstream teams choose simulation methods. New biology and institutions are authored working proposals; only explicit user premises are author canon. Numerical prototype outcomes are not silently promoted into natural laws.

entries.title: What is fixed, what is designed, what is experimental

fields.Author foundation: The sport is fast, competitive rad-roach circuit racing in a nuclear wasteland. The host can assimilate insect parts. The founding horn, mantis and hopper rivalry precedes the mature hobby by thirty years. Anyone can catch and breed. Wrangloids are hobbyists who make their expertise a livelihood. Open, Flyers, Fireworks and Speedsters retain the author’s class distinctions.
fields.Working world: Named donors, preparations, organizations, care practices and the anatomical explanations in this volume are current design proposals. They can be revised through an explicit amendment without deleting the useful history.
fields.Experimental record: A three-locus genome, six-animal patch, particular wallet, three event editions, two-roach solver or nine-by-six field describes a prior experiment. None limits the universe’s actual variety, population, wealth or sporting formats.
fields.Unknown: An unresolved size, lifespan, preservation time or calendar interval is not zero, infinite, forbidden or secretly selected. This volume supplies qualitative constraints where a useful definition is possible without invented calibration.

entries.title: Scope changes do not erase prior work

fields.Current priority: Develop the compendium’s living anatomy, component families, action vocabulary, selection objectives, commercial forms and shared institutions. The previous motion-code task is retained in the downstream implementation backlog, not marked complete.
fields.Preserved: Existing names, author canon, world records, reference evidence, trial histories and all previous wave data remain in the cumulative archive.
fields.New reading order: Read this volume for the present qualitative interpretation. Consult prior wave experiments for examples and their stated limits. An explicit W14 amendment takes precedence only for the named interpretation; it does not recalculate a saved racer or make an earlier simulation disappear.
fields.Completion claim: This volume completes the entries it contains at reference-definition scope. It is not a claim that every continent, faction, donor or game system has been fully authored.

fields.Preserved decision: Identity, native proportions, foundation, appearance and room for construction.
fields.Boundary: Changing shell paint is not changing a host; a brace is not the whole animal.

fields.Preserved decision: Grip, release, contact shape and surface-specific purchase.
fields.Boundary: A stepping foot is not a fixed wheel; higher adhesion is not identical to faster stepping.

fields.Preserved decision: Support and permitted deformation between mounted working anatomy.
fields.Boundary: Not general armor and not a second body-selection system.

fields.Preserved decision: Useful force, contraction cadence, efficiency and operating envelope.
fields.Boundary: Not stride length, reserve capacity, temperament or transmission ratio.

fields.Preserved decision: Convert available muscle work into useful stroke geometry and coordinated delivery.
fields.Boundary: Leverage changes force versus travel; synchronization changes timing. Neither creates power.

fields.Preserved decision: Stored energy, delivery ceiling, filling and working mass.
fields.Boundary: Capacity is not output; a fed donor is not proof of inherited capacity.

fields.Preserved decision: Limit a lean by contact, or detect it early enough for an existing actuator to respond.
fields.Boundary: A sensor alone cannot exert a stabilizing force.

fields.Preserved decision: Manage displacement and load during impact, then return the running geometry.
fields.Boundary: A landing joint is not automatically an active jump mechanism.

fields.Boundary: A passive foil is not a powered-flight wing system.

fields.Boundary: Appearance needs no hidden performance justification.

fields.Boundary: Simply adding soft tissue or ballast is not automatically damping.

fields.Boundary: No fabricated source-game slot is needed to legitimize these foundations.

entries.title: Sets and tiers are separate cataloguing systems

fields.Functional family: What a component does: drive, contact, reserve, support, guidance or another declared function.
fields.Preparation pattern: How anatomy has been arranged for use. One donor can supply alternate patterns; one pattern can be supplied by different suitable individuals.
fields.Performance qualification: A named protocol and its required properties. Hobby, Club, Circuit, Premier and Apex remain readable proposed bands, never genes or universal quality certificates.
fields.Availability: Standing stock, a scheduled brood release, a revived historic line, a one-off custom build or a commemorative tin. Scarcity can matter to a collector independently of race performance.
fields.Coordinated set: A selection of complementary physical components plus fitting knowledge. Matching names does not award an invisible aura.
fields.Distinct value: An improved component may genuinely outperform another at equal burden. An alternative ratio or reach may instead suit a different construction. Neither distinction should be erased to force all products into one ladder.

sections.title: 3. The living racer: common anatomical language
sections.intro: The host remains an animal whose working anatomy has been deliberately rebuilt. The following terms define what the builder is manipulating; they are not additional mandatory equipment slots.

fields.Definition: The persistent living roach that supplies the native foundation and receives grafts. Its identity continues through changes in equipment, finish, ownership and race career.
fields.Distinction: A build is a configuration of this animal; a saved build is not another animal.

fields.Definition: The native distribution of length, width, mass, articulation and root-bearing surfaces. Lowline, Needleback and Broadback are established working examples, not an exhaustive species list.
fields.Distinction: A narrow animal does not shrink bought limbs. Body-plan inheritance is a biology question, not a reason to copy the three-plan prototype globally.

fields.Definition: The proposed name for the rad roach’s mutable junction tissue. It incorporates donor anatomy and forms continuity with the host. It is an expression of the author’s assimilation premise.
fields.Distinction: The name does not require ordinary adult insects to molt, imply general limb regrowth, or restrict all grafting to a juvenile window.

fields.Definition: The interface through which a sect attaches and becomes supported, supplied and controlled. A root includes the tissues needed by its own function; different preparations expose different shapes.
fields.Distinction: The root is not an arbitrary colored socket that rejects another insect family.

fields.Definition: The portion of a construction that passes force from the working sect into adequate supporting anatomy. A horn root, wing hinge and leg root impose different directions of load.
fields.Distinction: A surface attachment that looks connected does not establish a useful load path.

fields.Definition: Contractile tissue plus the interfaces needed to apply its work. Mechanical output, control and supply must all reach the body part being driven.
fields.Distinction: Visible size, buzzing and species reputation do not individually establish useful output.

fields.Definition: Levers and coordinating junctions that define stroke travel, working force and timing. The native roach already has such structures.
fields.Distinction: The part that changes travel is not necessarily the part that synchronizes release.

fields.Definition: The actual anatomy touching a floor, wall, opponent or support. Material, area, orientation, loading and release all belong to its purpose.
fields.Distinction: Foot traction, rail sliding, gripping jaws and braking material are not a single universal grip score.

fields.Definition: The host and graft interfaces through which stored energy and necessary physiological support reach working tissues. The definition is functional; it does not assert a particular real-insect circulatory mechanism.
fields.Distinction: Separate organs cannot each spend the entire same reserve independently.

fields.Definition: The route by which a displaced limb, plate or moving mass returns to its useful position. It includes elastic, muscular or damped elements where those exist.
fields.Distinction: A spring can return energy; it does not automatically remove rebound or aim the returning limb.

fields.Definition: The connection between host control, local sensory information and a working graft. The shared host remains the actor; an installed arm does not bring an independent donor personality.
fields.Distinction: A sensor supplies information, not strength or omniscient knowledge of the course.

fields.Definition: A deliberately maintained release boundary around a graft root that supports reversible workshop rebuilding. It trades preparation and care for predictable swaps.
fields.Distinction: The collar helps reuse; it does not make assimilation possible in the first place, is not proprietary species permission, and does not guarantee every raw extraction is harmless.

entries.title: A functional installation has five kinds of continuity

fields.Attachment: The graft remains seated through its required movements.
fields.Support: Forces pass into the host rather than through a decorative or unsupported connection.
fields.Supply: The working anatomy receives the resources it requires and has unobstructed necessary exchange surfaces.
fields.Control: The host can activate, relax and interpret the graft to the extent required by the construction.
fields.Clearance: The working and returning anatomy has physical room to move.
fields.Example: A second drive bundle is meaningful when its supply and output can join a supported transmission. Simply attaching another muscle does not duplicate the entire leg system; conversely, a one-drive trial interface is not a universal law against multi-drive racers.
fields.Common experience: A coordinated beginner kit supplies an understandable arrangement that solves these requirements. Experts can redesign them. Every novice is not required to perform five repetitive diagnostic rituals before a first race.

entries.title: The body has regions, not an immutable equipment grid

fields.Brow and head: Good visibility and forward contact opportunities; horn or jaw load still needs a supported root. Split vanes may coexist around a central horn.
fields.Thorax: Working muscle, major load transfer and limb roots compete through actual anatomy. This is where bracing and controlled flexibility matter most.
fields.Flanks: Sensory stalks, articulated braces and rail guides need their own exposure, travel and support. Their working width may differ from folded width.
fields.Belly: Reservoir position, compliant landings, suspended masses and contact brakes interact through clearance and distribution.
fields.Abdomen: Storage and specialized glands affect distribution, supply and clearance. A rear weapon’s contents are not also available as the drive’s full fuel reserve.
fields.Dorsal envelope: Protective plates, vanes and powered wings need different opening and working spaces. Split armor can coexist with a flight root where its actual arrangement allows it.

entries.title: What the public performance readings mean

fields.Speed and acceleration: Pace and how quickly it is reached are outcomes of the working construction. They must remain desirable, intelligible comparisons; neither is a duplicate gene added on top of every contributing part.
fields.Grip and cornering: Grip describes contact behavior under specified conditions. Cornering describes the whole racer negotiating a route while maintaining useful motion. These values can correlate without being interchangeable.
fields.Balance: The construction’s ability to maintain or restore usable posture through sensing, support and action. It is not a universal reduction to all forms of damage.
fields.Hold-down: An aerodynamic load tied to motion and surface arrangement. Its authored RRR usefulness must remain tied to air interaction, not a standing-still buff.
fields.Mass and reserve: Actual carried material and available energy. Fill, hardware-like fixtures, living tissue and protection have distinguishable contributions.
fields.Observation discipline: A comparison names its load, surface, configuration and relevant condition. A measured lap is a result, not proof that one selected gene caused every improvement.

sections.title: 4. Sect reference catalogue: anatomy with a reason to exist
sections.intro: Each entry states its physical subject, useful selection, fitting contribution, visible behavior and commercial use. Familiar names are retained. Recovered earlier concepts are identified as reference designs rather than falsely counted as new implemented products. A product’s complete anatomical allocation governs whether two preparations can come from one donor; the same tissue cannot be sold twice.

fields.Donor and source: Furnace cicada; rooted pipe galleries, the Rooted signal pole and Root furnace. Adults supply working tissue; continued production needs the root-fed juvenile stage, not only an adult display cage.
fields.Prepared anatomy: A ribbed thoracic muscle bundle with supported ends and preserved supply/control interfaces. Its visible pulse becomes purposeful limb or wing-drive work after integration.
fields.Selection and breeding: Compare cadence under a declared load, useful force and conversion efficiency. Retain an efficient ordinary-cadence founder to complement a fast but hungry line. Noise and agitated movement are screening clues, not measurements.
fields.Builder contribution: Route work to a suitable linkage and choose leverage independently. Supply must support the desired duty, with space for the bundle to work without pinching surrounding anatomy.
fields.Visible racing consequence: Faster repeated working strokes when the rest of the build can use them. Foot-release bottlenecks or insufficient supply can prevent that output becoming pace.
fields.Hobby and trade: Useful in sprint kits and flight-drive preparations. Ordinary output supports club upgrades; selected economical tissue serves longer heats. A complete root nursery supports a recurring supplier.
fields.Boundary: It does not set leg reach or manufacture energy. The fictional Redline is not a claim that a real cicada’s sound-producing anatomy is a ready-made racing motor.

fields.Donor and source: Kilnback scarab; protected furnace compost and Cooling compost. Retain healthy adults and complete grub/pupal development for repeat production.
fields.Prepared anatomy: Dense muscle columns with broad working attachments. The prepared block needs supporting anatomy capable of receiving its repeated load.
fields.Selection and breeding: Select useful force per material mass and sustained force under the intended operating demand. Large shell size is not sufficient. Frame traits from the same line are a separate product objective.
fields.Builder contribution: Place the bundle near a practical output path and choose the gait ratio. A loaded body may need structural reinforcement; an empty decorative plate does not supply it.
fields.Visible racing consequence: Forceful starts, climbing work and recovery after traffic when contact can transmit the force. Higher-force tissue need not have the highest unloaded cadence.
fields.Hobby and trade: Loaded Open constructions, rough-course kits and drive commissions. Disjoint internal support plates can support a separate Boxbrace preparation where the harvest plan preserves them.
fields.Boundary: A forceful drive does not automatically make a charge effective: approach, contact and horn-root support remain necessary.

fields.Donor and source: Ballast mole cricket; Ballast trench, Ballast Banks and suitable loose root beds. Hip structure, toes and sleeve tissue have different allocation purposes.
fields.Prepared anatomy: Short hip levers and their working junctions, prepared to exchange stroke distance for force at the driven limbs.
fields.Selection and breeding: Select the mechanical-advantage range required by the intended construction and consistent joint geometry. Do not select maximum ratio as a universal optimum. A modest ratio with good articulation may fit the product better.
fields.Builder contribution: Choose the working ratio through preparation and fine alignment. Match travel with the installed muscle and running spars rather than adding a second stride bonus.
fields.Visible racing consequence: Shorter forceful strokes, useful starts and load handling. Extended clean straights may expose its limited travel per drive cycle.
fields.Hobby and trade: Loaded kit production; hip assemblies sold separately from cleats. A breeder can supply a repeated geometry range rather than an alleged top-tier gene.
